messages.content:
Diagnosis:
The test `testInfiniteLoop()` fails because the `HelpFormatter` class hangs in an infinite loop when formatting help text with long descriptions that do not fit on a single line given the configured width (20 characters in this case). According to the current bug report, if a word is longer than the available width, the wrapping code goes into an infinite loop until the JVM crashes with OutOfMemoryError.

Examining the `HelpFormatter` code, the infinite loop happens in the `renderWrappedText` method, which is responsible for line-wrapping the help text descriptions. This method uses `findWrapPos` to find a wrap position up to the given width. If no wrap position is found (`pos == -1`), it appends the remaining text and exits. Otherwise, it appends the substring up to the wrap position and continues.

However, the critical bug is detected in the loop starting on line 822 of `renderWrappedText`. The loop updates the text by trimming and padding and recalculates `pos`. If the next wrap position `pos` is equal to the previous value `lastPos`, it means the substring is not advancing (the wrap position has not changed). This causes the method to throw a runtime exception to avoid infinite looping, as shown on line 836.

The test fails because previously this exception was not thrown and the code entered an infinite loop. The test description suggests the infinite loop manifested before this check was added, and now the code tries to detect this condition and throw a meaningful exception.

In summary:
- The infinite loop occurs because the text to be wrapped has a word longer than the available width.
- `renderWrappedText` tries to wrap the text, but the wrap position does not advance because the word cannot fit.
- The code now throws an exception to avoid infinite loops, but in the past, this caused a hang.
- The test case triggers this exact condition by setting a small width and using an option description with a very long word.

No related fixes are apparent in the recent bug reports, so this appears to be an isolated issue with text wrapping in `HelpFormatter`.

The root cause is in `renderWrappedText` method's wrapping logic that cannot handle words longer than the wrap width gracefully, causing infinite loops previously and now throwing an exception.

This matches the behavior described in the bug report and the failure of the test case.

The best location for a fix is likely in `HelpFormatter.renderWrappedText` to either ensure words longer than the width break properly or be handled differently so that infinite loops or exceptions do not occur.

Suggested: review `findWrapPos` as well, which determines where to wrap text.
Title: Diagnosis
Details: The infinite loop happens in the HelpFormatter when printing help for options whose description contains words longer than the configured width. The test triggers this by setting width=20 and adding an option with a very long description word. Inside HelpFormatter, the printHelp method calls printOptions which calls renderOptions and then renderWrappedText. The renderWrappedText method tries to find wrap positions and break text lines accordingly. However, if a single word is longer than the width, the wrap position does not advance and the loop keeps processing the same text segment repeatedly, causing infinite looping until an OutOfMemoryError occurs. The recent code snippet shows that now renderWrappedText has a check to throw an exception if the wrap position does not advance to avoid infinite loops. This is the exact issue described in the bug report and failing test. The root cause lies in renderWrappedText's inability to gracefully handle words longer than the specified line width, causing stalled wrap positions and infinite loops.

Recommended fix location:
HelpFormatter.renderWrappedText(StringBuffer,int,int,String)

Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
